title: Suppress the selected quadratic response at large balanced impulse
statement: For the preceding exact second variation let I(xi)=integral_0^5 exp(i xi G(z))dz and L=AT. On fifteen quadratic/linear profile pieces, elementary split-at-|xi|^-1/2 and integration by parts give |I(xi)|<=32/sqrt(|xi|) for xi!=0. Substitution into the exact full-Euler coefficient yields ||w2(5T)||2<=32sqrt(2pi)T/sqrt(|AT|), hence<=32sqrt(2pi)2^(-11n/2) for A=2^(8n),T=2^(-3n). Nonzero small-impulse echo defect and vanishing large-impulse coefficient are compatible. This verifies ONE explicit nonlinear interaction; it does not estimate the entire averaged transformed bilinear operator, all resonances or higher iterates. The example first variation remains unchanged by the inviscid shear, so coefficient suppression alone is not total-velocity contraction.
